_comment: Hand-authored half of the identity source card. The derived half -- node
labels, node properties, relationship types and endpoints -- is generated
from the ReliaQuest catalog by utils/kg_builder/catalog/card.py. This file
carries only what no catalog can supply: connection details, safety limits,
provenance, and what each label and edge MEANS to an analyst.
The glosses are load-bearing rather than decorative. With 72 labels including
six different flavours of 'group' (GROUP, ENTRA_GROUP, OKTA_GROUP, GCP_GROUP,
AWS_SSO_GROUP, AWS_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP) and a real ENTRA_LICENCE/ENTRA_LICENSE
spelling collision, these descriptions are the deterministic planner's only
disambiguation signal when a question says 'group'.

provenance.source_name: ReliaQuest customer identity graph (schema); synthetic tenant (instances)
provenance.id_scheme: mixed — GUID, Windows SID, UPN, AWS ARN, Okta base-62, GCP resource path
provenance.caveat: The schema is real and unmodified. The instances are generated and conform to it structurally. Any claim from this source is about schema navigation, never about detection quality on a real tenant.

nodes.AD_CERT_TEMPLATE: An Active Directory Certificate Services template defining what a certificate may be issued for and who may enrol. Misconfigured templates are the ESC1-ESC8 privilege-escalation family.
nodes.AD_ENTERPRISE_CA: An enterprise Certificate Authority trusted by the forest to issue certificates.
nodes.AD_ISSUANCE_POLICY: A certificate issuance policy OID constraining which templates a CA may issue.
nodes.AWS_ACTION: A single AWS IAM action (for example s3:GetObject) referenced by a policy statement.
nodes.AWS_EC2_ROUTE_TABLE: An EC2 route table governing traffic direction within a VPC.
nodes.AWS_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP: A stateful EC2 network firewall rule set. Despite the name this is a NETWORK control and never an identity principal — it is not a group of users.
nodes.AWS_EC2_SUBNET: A subnet within an EC2 VPC.
nodes.AWS_INTERNET_GATEWAY: A VPC internet gateway providing outbound public reachability.
nodes.AWS_ORGANIZATION: An AWS Organizations root tying member accounts under shared policy.
nodes.AWS_POLICY: An IAM policy document, managed or inline, granting or denying actions.
nodes.AWS_ROLE: An IAM role assumable by a principal, keyed by an ARN. The usual target of cross-account privilege escalation.
nodes.AWS_SAML_PROVIDER: A SAML identity provider registered with IAM for federated sign-in.
nodes.AWS_SERVICE: An AWS service principal that may assume a role or be named in a trust policy.
nodes.AWS_SSO_GROUP: A group defined in AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO). An identity principal — distinct from AWS_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP, which is a network control.
nodes.AWS_SSO_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP: The membership record joining an AWS_SSO_USER to an AWS_SSO_GROUP.
nodes.AWS_SSO_INSTANCE: An AWS IAM Identity Center instance for a tenant.
nodes.AWS_SSO_USER: A user provisioned into AWS IAM Identity Center.
nodes.AWS_STATEMENT: One statement inside an IAM policy: effect, actions, resources, conditions.
nodes.AWS_TRUST_PRINCIPAL: A principal named in a role's trust policy as permitted to assume it.
nodes.AWS_TRUST_STATEMENT: One statement of a role's assume-role trust policy.
nodes.AWS_VPC: A virtual private cloud network boundary.
nodes.CONTAINER: An Active Directory container object holding other directory objects. Structural, unlike an OU it cannot have a GPO linked to it.
nodes.DEVICE: A computer account — workstation, server, or domain controller — in Active Directory, Entra, or a cloud instance inventory.
nodes.DOMAIN: An Active Directory domain, the root of a directory partition and the target of replication rights such as DC_SYNC.
nodes.ENTRA_ADMINISTRATIVE_UNIT: An Entra ID administrative unit scoping directory-role assignments to a subset of the tenant.
nodes.ENTRA_APPLICATION: An Entra ID application registration — the definition of an app, distinct from the ENTRA_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL that instantiates it in a tenant.
nodes.ENTRA_APP_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT: An assignment granting a principal an application role exposed by an Entra application.
nodes.ENTRA_AUTHENTICATION_METHOD: An authentication method registered to an Entra identity (FIDO2 key, authenticator app, phone).
nodes.ENTRA_CONDITIONAL_ACCESS_POLICY: A Conditional Access policy gating sign-in on conditions such as location, device state, or risk.
nodes.ENTRA_CROSS_TENANT_PARTNER: Another Entra tenant with a cross-tenant access configuration.
nodes.ENTRA_DELEGATED_GRANT: An OAuth2 delegated permission grant letting an application act for a signed-in user.
nodes.ENTRA_DIRECTORY_ROLE: A built-in or custom Entra directory role such as Global Administrator.
nodes.ENTRA_DOMAIN: A DNS domain verified against an Entra tenant. Distinct from DOMAIN, which is an on-premises Active Directory domain.
nodes.ENTRA_FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL: A federated identity credential permitting workload-identity federation without a stored secret.
nodes.ENTRA_GROUP: A group in Entra ID, cloud-native or synchronised from on-premises. Distinct from GROUP, which is the on-premises Active Directory security group.
nodes.ENTRA_LICENCE: A licence assigned in Entra ID. NOTE: the delivered catalog declares BOTH this spelling and ENTRA_LICENSE as separate node types. This is a real collision in the customer's production catalog, preserved verbatim rather than merged. A question about licences may be genuinely ambiguous between the two, and the honest response is to say so.
nodes.ENTRA_LICENSE: A licence assigned in Entra ID. See the note on ENTRA_LICENCE: both spellings exist as distinct declared node types in the delivered catalog.
nodes.ENTRA_NAMED_LOCATION: A named network location (IP range or country) referenced by Conditional Access policies.
nodes.ENTRA_PERMISSION: A permission (scope or app role) that an Entra application may request or hold.
nodes.ENTRA_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT: An assignment binding a principal to an ENTRA_DIRECTORY_ROLE, optionally scoped to an administrative unit.
nodes.ENTRA_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL: The tenant-local instance of an Entra application, holding the credentials and permissions the app actually exercises.
nodes.ENTRA_TENANT: An Entra ID tenant, the top-level boundary of a Microsoft cloud identity estate.
nodes.GCP_BINDING: An IAM binding tying a member to a role on a Google Cloud resource. Bindings are where GCP privilege actually lives.
nodes.GCP_GROUP: A Google Cloud identity group. Distinct from GROUP (on-premises Active Directory) and ENTRA_GROUP (Microsoft cloud).
nodes.GCP_LOG_SINK: A logging sink exporting Cloud Logging entries to a destination.
nodes.GCP_NODE_POOL: A node pool within a GKE cluster, which runs as a service account.
nodes.GCP_PERMISSION: A single Google Cloud IAM permission contained by a role.
nodes.GCP_PROJECT: A Google Cloud project, the usual boundary for resources and IAM policy.
nodes.GCP_ROLE: A Google Cloud IAM role, predefined or custom, holding a set of permissions.
nodes.GPO: A Group Policy Object. Its power comes from where it is linked (GP_LINK): write access to a GPO linked to a domain or OU is code execution on everything below it.
nodes.GROUP: An on-premises Active Directory security group. The dominant privilege carrier in this schema — 48 of the 60 declared relationship triples originate here. Distinct from ENTRA_GROUP, OKTA_GROUP, GCP_GROUP and AWS_SSO_GROUP (cloud identity groups) and from AWS_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP (a network control).
nodes.OKTA_API_SERVICE_INTEGRATION: An Okta API service integration holding scoped API access.
nodes.OKTA_API_TOKEN: An Okta API token. A bearer credential — possession is authorisation.
nodes.OKTA_APPLICATION: An application integrated with Okta for single sign-on.
nodes.OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET: A client secret issued to an Okta OAuth application.
nodes.OKTA_CUSTOM_ROLE: A custom administrator role in Okta defining a permission set.
nodes.OKTA_DEVICE: A device registered with Okta. Distinct from DEVICE, which is the Active Directory or cloud computer account.
nodes.OKTA_GROUP: A group in Okta, often the unit of application assignment. Distinct from GROUP (on-premises Active Directory).
nodes.OKTA_JWK: A JSON Web Key registered for an Okta application's private-key authentication.
nodes.OKTA_ORGANIZATION: An Okta org — the tenant boundary of an Okta identity estate.
nodes.OKTA_PERMISSION: A single permission contained by an Okta role.
nodes.OKTA_RESOURCE_SET: A set of resources an Okta custom role may be exercised over.
nodes.OKTA_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT: An assignment binding an Okta principal to a role over a resource set.
nodes.ORGANIZATION: The top-level organisational entity for a customer estate.
nodes.OU: An Active Directory organisational unit. Unlike CONTAINER, a GPO can be linked to an OU, which is why OU write access is an escalation path.
nodes.USER: A user account — Active Directory, Entra, Okta, or cloud. The most attribute-rich label in this schema at 131 declared attributes.

relationships.ADD_KEY_CREDENTIAL_LINK: The principal may write msDS-KeyCredentialLink on the target, allowing a certificate to be attached and the target impersonated. The 'shadow credentials' technique.
relationships.ALL_EXTENDED_RIGHTS: The principal holds every extended right on the target, including password reset and, on a domain, the replication rights that constitute DCSync.
relationships.APP_ASSIGNMENT: The user is assigned an application, granting sign-in to it.
relationships.APPLIES_FROM: The Conditional Access policy takes effect from the named location.
relationships.BOUND_BY: The principal is bound to a Google Cloud IAM binding, receiving whatever role that binding grants.
relationships.DC_SYNC: The principal holds the combination of replication rights that allows replicating directory secrets from the domain — every password hash, including krbtgt. Effective domain compromise.
relationships.GENERIC_ALL: Full control over the target object. Subsumes every other ACL right in this schema.
relationships.GENERIC_WRITE: The principal may write any non-protected attribute of the target, which usually suffices for takeover.
relationships.GET_CHANGES: One half of the DCSync right pair. Alone it is insufficient; combined with GET_CHANGES_ALL it is DCSync.
relationships.GET_CHANGES_ALL: The second half of the DCSync right pair, permitting replication of secret attributes.
relationships.GET_CHANGES_IN_FILTERED_SET: Replication of the filtered attribute set, relevant to RODC-related escalation.
relationships.GP_LINK: The Group Policy Object is linked to the target domain or OU, so its settings apply to everything beneath it.
relationships.MEMBER_OF: The principal belongs to the group, inheriting its privileges. NOTE: in this source the USER->GROUP, GROUP->GROUP and USER->ENTRA_GROUP forms are INFERRED by the research project rather than declared by the customer catalog, whose export dropped attribute-less edges. The USER->OKTA_GROUP and USER->GCP_GROUP forms are declared.
relationships.OWNS: The principal owns the target object and can therefore rewrite its ACL at will. Ownership is equivalent to full control.
relationships.RUNS_AS: The device or node pool executes under the identity of the target account, so compromise of the host yields that account.
relationships.SAME_FOREST_TRUST: The two domains share a forest. Intra-forest trust is not a security boundary — the forest is.
relationships.TRUSTED_BY: The source domain is trusted by the target domain, so principals from the source may be authorised in the target.
relationships.WRITE_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTIONS: The principal may write account restriction attributes, enabling delegation-based escalation.
relationships.WRITE_DACL: The principal may rewrite the target's access control list, and can therefore grant itself any other right. Equivalent to full control in two steps.
relationships.WRITE_GP_LINK: The principal may change which Group Policy Objects are linked to the OU, and so what code runs on everything beneath it.
relationships.WRITE_OWNER: The principal may take ownership of the target, and an owner may rewrite the ACL. Equivalent to full control in three steps.
